chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a house that fell upon a group of people together, so it is not known which of them died first. He said: 'One inherits from the other.' I said: 'Indeed Abu Hanifah included something in it.' He said: 'And what did he include?' I said: 'If two brothers, one of whom is my mawla (freedman) and the other is a mawla of a man, one of them has one hundred thousand dirhams and the other has nothing, they boarded a ship and drowned, and it is not known which of them died first, then the wealth belongs to the heirs of the one who has nothing, and the heirs of the one who has the wealth have nothing.' He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I have heard it, and it is so.' I said: 'And if two slaves, I freed one of them and you freed the other, one of them has one hundred thousand dirhams and the other has nothing,' he said the same.
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed when multiple people die in the same accident and the order of death is unknown?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the principle of mutual inheritance among simultaneous deceased parties, specifically endorsing the view that the heir of the poorer deceased inherits from the richer one, a ruling he confirms he had previously heard. This narration highlights the Shia jurisprudential stance against the Hanafi approach of suspending inheritance until the order of death is determined, emphasizing the immediate transfer of wealth to the surviving heirs based on the presumption of simultaneous death.
